texts.facts: The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident dated 21.12.2022. 2. The accident caused due to the negligence of the rider of the motorbike. The respondent No.1 being the Insurer and the respondent No.2 being the RC owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. It has denied the entire averments of the petition except admitting the issuance of "Private Motor 2 Wheeler Policy" bearing No.POPMW00100607445 in favour of the second respondent in respect of motorbike bearing Reg.No.KA-42-Y- 4575 and it is valid from 21.01.2022 to 20.0.2023 and their liability. The petition is bad for non compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act. The petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties. It has denied the occurrence of the accident and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-Y-4575. The rider of the offending vehicle did Ramesh Naika vs Sbi General Ins Co Ltd on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67497805/ 2 not have valid DL as on the date of accident. He has denied the petitioner averments except admitting that his vehicle was insured with the 1 st respondent and he was the RC owner of the motorbike. The Policy valid from 21.01.2022 to 20.01.2023 which is in force as on the date of accident. The rider of the motorcycle has a valid and effective DL as on the date of accident.

6. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:-
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 21.12.2022 at 12.26 to 12.27, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of Splendor Plus bike vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-Y-4575 and in the said accident petitioner sustained
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.
What order or award?

On the other side,
the Respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any documents on its behalf.

On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows:-
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2: In the Affirmative,
Issue No.3:

As per the final order,
 for the following:-
 REASONS

10. Issue No.1:-
Ramesh Naika vs Sbi General Ins Co Ltd on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67497805/
3

In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the Splendor Plus Bike bearing Reg.No.KA-42-Y-4575, the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 and produced 7 documents as per Exs.P.
He has reiterated the contents of the petition in his affidavit filed in lieu of his chief examination.
During the cross examination of PW.1, he has stated that Mr.Prakash C was riding the motorcycle in which he was going.
He was going from Hosadurga to Kanakapura.
The Road was a Tar Rad and is big enough for two lorries to move.
There was no vehicle in front of their vehicle and there was no vehicle in front of offending vehicle.
Further admitted that both the motorcycles suffered damages to the front portion and the accident was a head on collision.

The respondent No.1 denied that the accident caused due to the negligence of the rider of the offending motorcycle and contended that there was sole negligence on the part of the rider of the petitioner's motorcycle.
11. The FIR was registered on the complaint of petitioner on the next day of the accident i.e., on 22.12.2022 and the accident occurred on 21.12.2022.
Ex. P.2
spot mahazar and seizure mahazar was conducted on 23.12.2022 at about 12.30 to 01.15pm and at about 11.00 to 11.45am.
Ex. P.3
IMV report shows that the motorcycle in which the petitioner was proceeding damaged its head light cover scratched, crash guard, clutch lever, rear body and tail lamp damaged.
Similarly the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-42-Y- 4575 damaged to its front right side indicator, front registration number plate, crash guard damaged.
Ex . P.4
is the notice issued to the RC owner of the offending vehicle regarding the details of the accident and the involvement of the vehicle, place and manner of accident.
Ex.P.5 is the Wound Certificate which shows that the petitioner has suffered injuries in an RTA on 21.12.2022 at about 12.15pm.
Ex.P.7 is the charge sheet filed against the rider of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-Y-4575 after thorough investigation.
As against this the respondent Nos.1 & 2 have contended that the vehicle was not involved in the accident.

However,
the respondents did not produce any document nor examined any witness in support of their contention to prove the negligence of the petitioner.
Therefore the Tribunal holds that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the Splendor Plus Bike vehicle bearing No.KA-42-Y-4575.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:-
In order to prove the injuries and disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner has produced the wound certificate as per Ex.P.5.
As per Ex.P.5, the Petitioner has sustained (i) Pain in left shoulder, (ii) Restriction of movements in left shoulder.
He was diagnosed with fractures of middle 1/3rd of clavicle and treatment was given which are grievous in nature.
13. The petitioner has also got examined Dr.Chidananda K.J.C. as PW.2.

He has deposed that the petitioner has suffered left mid 1/3rd clavicle fracture and left GT proximal humerus fracture and petitioner underwent conservative management and assessed the whole body disability at 9.66%.
He has also produced Exs.P.10 & P.11 i.e., OPD record and X-ray.
During his cross examination he has stated that he has not treated the petitioner.
The petitioner was conservatively treated for all the injuries suffered.
Fractures are united.
There are no complications at the fractures site.
Further stated that clavicle bone is supporting bone to the shoulder joint.

The petitioner has not separated Ramesh Naika vs Sbi General Ins Co Ltd on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67497805/
4 the disability for clavicle and humerus.
There is no physical disability as such for clavicle.
On perusal of the X-ray and other records, it appears that there was a fracture of left mid 1/3rd clavicle fracture and left GT proximal humerus fractures.
PW.2 stated that the injuries are permanent in nature, this will have difficulty in doing daily routine activities.
The petitioner claims to be a Coolie.

Therefore,
this Tribunal deems it fit to fix the whole body disability at 9.66%.

Monthly income:
14.
The Petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, he was doing Coolie work and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
In support of this he has not produced any documents like bank statement etc., nor examined any witness.
The accident occurred in the year 2022.
Therefore, this court deems it fit to fix the notional income of the deceased at Rs.15,500/- per month.
15. At the time of accident the Petitioner was aged about 42 years as could be made out from Ex.P.8/Notarized copy of Aadhar Card.
He was hale and healthy before the accident.
The accident took place in the year 2022.

Keeping all the above things in mind, Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation:-
 i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:-

After the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to Hosadurga Primary Health Center and thereafter to Kanakapura Spandana Pvt. Diagnostic Centre and thereafter shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital wherein he was admitted as an inpatient.
Considering that the nature of injuries he has undergone are grievous and simple, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.60,000/- under this head.
ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:

The Petitioner has pleaded that he has spent a sum of huge amount towards treatment, medicines,
conveyance, food and nourishment and other incidental expenses etc.
In this regard, the petitioner has produced medical bills for Rs.2,928/- as per Ex.P.9.
There is no contrary evidence produced by the Respondent.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the said amount under this head.

iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:-
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
In this regard petitioner has not produced discharge summary of any hospitals wherein the petitioner was treated as an inpatient.
Therefore, considering the nature of injuries it can be said that the Petitioner may have required at least one month time for recovering from the injuries suffered by him.
Hence, he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.15,500/- under this head.

iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:-
Ramesh Naika vs Sbi General Ins Co Ltd on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67497805/
5
On perusal of Ex.P.8, the date of birth of the petitioner is 01.01.1980 and the date of accident is 21.12.2022.
Therefore, as on the date of the accident the Petitioner's age is 42 years.
As per the dictum laid down in Sarala Verma's case, above 42 years the appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 14.
As such the petitioner is entitled to Rs.2,51,546/-.

(v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND  HAPPINESS:-
The Petitioner was aged about 42 years at the time of accident.
He has sustained grievous injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 9.66% functional disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his life.
Because of this he will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts.
Therefore, considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered, a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head.
(vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT CHARGES:
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above said hospitals, admitted as an inpatient and discharged with advise.
However, during this period he must have spent considerable amount on his food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant expenses.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.

16. The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain and suffering Rs.60,000/-
2. Medical Expenses Rs.2,928/-
3. Loss of income during laid up Rs.15,500/-
period 4. Loss of Future Income Rs.2,51,546/-

5 . Loss of future amenities and Rs.20,000/-
happiness 6. Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.20,000/-
nourishment charges TOTAL Rs.3,69,974/-
If it rounded off it comes to Rs.3,70,000/- and same is awarded under different heads to the Petitioner.
Liability 17.
The Respondents have not proved their defence as discussed above.
Therefore, the Respondents being the Insurer and the Owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
However, as the policy existed as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1/insurer has to indemnify the respondent No.2/insured and has to pay compensation awarded to the petitioner.

The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.10,00,000/-
but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.3,70,000/- with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is held in the affirmative.
18. Issue No.3:-

For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition is allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,70,000/- (Rupees Three Lakhs Seventy Thousand only) from the Respondents along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation to the petitioner.
However, the Respondent No.1/Insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award.
On deposit of compensation and interest, entire amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner by way of e-payment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per rules

. 
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw decree accordingly.
